title: Getting Started
summary: Join a server, pick a map, choose a job and get on the road.

blocks.text: Car Driving Indonesia is a town-and-city driving and roleplay experience set on an ever-growing map of Indonesia. It is free to play on Roblox, and game passes are optional.

items: Open the official experience on Roblox (place 6911148748, published by the verified CDID Studio Official Group) and press Play.
Pick a map. Jakarta, Jawa Barat, Jawa Tengah, Jawa Timur and Bali are all part of the same experience, and seasonal maps appear during events.
Open Job Selection at your map's spawn point to choose a job. Each job gives you its uniform and a work vehicle at the start location.
Earn rupiah (Rp) from jobs, then visit a dealership to buy a car of your own.
Use CDID Trans buildings to fast-travel between places. The wiki lists the fee as Rp 1,000,000 per teleport.

blocks.text: If a server shuts down, the developers say it means a server fix or an update is being applied.

title: Buying Vehicles
summary: How CDID's showrooms, brand names, game passes and garage slots work.

blocks.text: Cars are bought with in-game rupiah at dealerships around the map. Brands use in-game names modelled on real manufacturers; the community wiki lists Tokoma for Toyota, Honade for Honda, Densu for Daihatsu and Mestibis for Mitsubishi, among others.

items: Brand dealerships (Tokoma, Honade, Hyunson, Densu and more) sell that brand's current line-up.
Sumber Jaya Used Cars sells second-hand models from many brands and eras.
The Premium Dealership and Otnas Esprit Works Cafe carry luxury, exotic and enthusiast cars.
The Retro Cars Dealership specialises in classics.
The Komercial Dealership sells trucks, buses and vans.

blocks.text: Some cars need a game pass before you can buy them: Luxury Car (R$259), Rare Imports (R$189), Retro Car (R$169) or Emergency Vehicle (R$139). The vehicle catalogue on this site shows which pass each car needs.
Garage space is limited. The Additional Ownable Car pass (R$99) adds 28 car slots, and 2x Additional Ownable Car (R$269) adds more.
Browse the vehicle catalogue

title: Dealership Guide
summary: Which showroom sells what, and where to find it.

blocks.text: Jakarta has most of the brand showrooms: Tokoma, Liaxe, Mestibis, Buffermacht/BMR, Murceso-Venz, Hyunson and Wuliuz. Bekasi has commercial, Hyunson, CIA and Sumber Jaya dealers. The wiki places Honade, Sanziky, Otnas Esprit Works and a Sumber Jaya branch in Bandung, and Ciawi has a single Densu dealer.
The wiki's map article was last edited in July 2025, before the Jawa Timur map (V2.2.0) and the Bandung rework (V2.7). Some showrooms may have moved.
Open the dealership locator

title: Vehicle Customisation
summary: Modification garages, the Advanced Modification pass, and how to tune your car.

blocks.text: Modification garages, including those in Sentul and Jakarta, let you customise cars. Updates have expanded the options over time: lights, horn and reset (V1.2.5), the modification feature itself (V1.9), a new modification UI (V2.0) and tyre modification (V2.2.0 and V2.3).

The Advanced Modification pass (R$249) unlocks custom colour, custom plate, speed-limiter delete and air suspension. According to the wiki, players who already owned the older separate passes get it cheaper, and owners of all three get it free.
Car washes in Jakarta, BSD and Bali clean dirty vehicles.

title: Limited, Exclusive & Event Vehicles
summary: Timed releases, the Weekly Car Drop, exclusive unit counts, points rewards and minigame boxes.

blocks.text: Many CDID cars are only sold for a short time. The community limited-car log records several ways they are released:

items: Timed limiteds: on sale for a fixed window after an update, usually 2–12 hours and sometimes only 5 minutes.
Weekly Car Drop: introduced in V2.2.0. A new set of limited cars is released each week.
Exclusive cars: introduced in V2.3 and sold in fixed unit counts, for example 500 units with short restocks.
Event rewards: earned with event points (Ramadhan, Eid al-Adha, V5 Nostalgia, Independence Day) or given away during an event.
Minigame boxes: some cars only come from boxes earned through minigames.

blocks.text: See limited vehicles in the catalogue

title: Gacha System
summary: What is confirmed about the new gacha system in V2.8.

blocks.text: The V2.8 changelog officially lists a "New Gacha System". The community wiki already lists Minigame Box, Limited Box and Robux Box as sources of some cars.
Odds, prices and the full prize pool have not been published in a source we could access. This guide will be updated once they are documented. Until then, check the official Discord.

items: Toll roads, including the Gerbang Tol Cikampek Utama toll plaza. The toll system was reworked in V2.4.

Automatic headlamps and self-cancelling turn signals, added in V2.3.
A speedometer UI redesigned in V2.0, and a minimap reworked in V2.2.0.
A phone system, reworked in V2.4.

blocks.text: CDID follows the Indonesian calendar. Recent official changelogs list these events:

items: Ramadhan: a quest in V2.0, then a seasonal map and race event in V2.5.5.
Eid al-Adha: in V2.6, with commercial-vehicle rewards.
Independence Day (17 August): HUT RI 78 in V1.2.5, then V2.2.0 and the Bandung event in V2.7.
Halloween: V1.9, V2.3 and the Halloween Event 2026 in V2.8.
Christmas: V2.4, with a limited-time map.
Partner and nostalgia events: myBCA in V2.7 and V5 Nostalgia 2026 in V2.6.5.
